purpose: Fixed sentences describing what each kit check requires. They are given to the repair stage beside the failing IDs and JSON paths, so a repair sees the requirement without ever seeing raw tool output.

checks.KT-BI-01: bible.json must exist and match the bible schema.
checks.KT-BI-02: Each named person uses a seeded name spelled exactly, or a replacement that passes the name rules: distinct initials, distinct sound keys, plain ASCII, not on a ban list. The cast size must equal the seeded cast size.
checks.KT-BI-03: Respect the cognitive budget: suspect count within limits, locations, critical strings and total cast at or under the caps.
checks.KT-BI-04: Every option must be supported by at least two facts, and every cited fact must exist.
checks.KT-BI-05: Every question must have exactly one correct option.
checks.KT-BI-06: The red herring must target a wrong option, belong to a suspect who is not the culprit, rest on an existing fact of kind secondary, and name existing refuting facts.
checks.KT-BI-07: The aha list must use exactly the seeded patterns; mask, reframe and conclusion facts must exist and be three different facts.
checks.KT-BI-08: Every named person needs a complete person sheet and at least the minimum number of relationships to other named people.
checks.KT-BI-09: A person sheet uses quirk vocabulary. Replace decoration with pressure, attention or habit that changes behaviour.
checks.KT-BI-10: The bible uses a stock trope it has not declared. Either rework it so it grows from this world, or embrace it on purpose: list it in premise.tropes_embraced with a lens. Soft warning.
checks.KT-BI-11: Exactly one culprit, who is a suspect; the method and motive facts must be solution-critical.
checks.KT-BI-12: The setting needs at least the minimum textures, internal terms and rhythms.
checks.KT-BI-13: Critical strings must equal the seeded values exactly and each must have a meaning.
checks.KT-BI-14: All IDs must match the opaque ID grammar and be unique.
checks.KT-PL-01: case.json, skin.json and clue_plan.json must exist, parse as JSON, and the plan must match the plan schema.
checks.KT-PL-02: Every solution-critical fact needs the minimum number of routes, two of them sharing no document, and at least one route made only of search-free documents.
checks.KT-PL-03: No single document may carry every supporting fact of a correct option.
checks.KT-PL-04: The herring needs an inducing document at an early tier, a document establishing the secondary secret, and refuting documents at a later tier than the inducing one.
checks.KT-PL-05: The masking document must sit at an earlier tier than the reframing document, and no document may list the aha conclusion fact.
checks.KT-PL-06: Each suspect must appear in enough documents, written by enough different authors, including one document with no solution-critical fact.
checks.KT-PL-07: Use known document forms, at least the minimum number of distinct forms, and no single form above the maximum share.
checks.KT-PL-08: Every document needs an author who is a named person or a department, an intended reader, and an in-world reason.
checks.KT-PL-09: Each department must use a different seeded voice profile, within the department cap.
checks.KT-PL-10: Placeholders must follow the format, belong to a known owner, appear exactly once as a whole string in case.json, carry only facts their document holds, and no unlisted placeholder may appear.
checks.KT-PL-11: World documents must stay within the share range, each must involve a named person, carry no solution-critical fact, and every world placeholder must have a word limit at or under the flavor cap.
checks.KT-PL-12: case.json must reuse the bible's IDs for people, solution-critical facts, questions and options.
checks.KT-PL-13: Every critical string must be required by at least one placeholder.
checks.KT-PL-14: Every planned document ID must appear in case.json, and no document ID may repeat.
checks.KT-PL-15: Every fact ID used in the plan must exist in the bible.
checks.KT-FL-01: fill.json must match the fill schema, name its owner, and fill exactly the owner's placeholders.
checks.VL-01: Remove signposting phrases and puzzle vocabulary from player-facing text.
checks.VL-02: A stock name appears. Use only the seeded cast names.
checks.VL-03: Remove machine-prose phrases; carry the meaning with a particular instead.
checks.VL-04: Within each question, option texts must be within the length tolerance of their mean.
checks.VL-05: Every option text must name a real person or location from the case.
checks.VL-06: Each required critical string must appear verbatim in its text.
checks.VL-07: A findings text must contain no assessment language.
checks.VL-08: An assessment text must follow its voice profile: sentence length band, first-person rule, hedge rule and bias markers.
checks.VL-09: Two documents by different owners share too many identical word sequences. Rewrite in the author's own voice.
checks.VL-10: Remove confession phrasing. No document may admit the act outright.
checks.VL-11: Each text may claim only facts assigned to its placeholder, and must claim every fact assigned.
checks.VL-12: A text exceeds its word limit, or is empty.
checks.VL-14: Quirk vocabulary appears in player-facing text.
checks.VL-15: Too many dashes or not-just-but constructions for the archive's register.
checks.VL-16: A word is one letter away from a cast name. Spell names exactly.
checks.KT-RV-01: review.json must contain an integer score in range for every SECOND-MODEL rubric item, flags from the failure-mode list only, and no text.
checks.KT-RN-02: Engine schema or vocabulary changed since this run started. Run compat_check and start a new run.
checks.KT-BI-15: Every named person needs a voice sample within the word limits, free of banned phrases, that asserts no case fact.
checks.KT-PL-16: The number of documents must be within the document range for this build.
checks.KT-PL-17: Documents must use at least the minimum number of tiers, so the case has an intake, an impasse and a reframing.
checks.KT-PL-18: Every world document declares its purpose: it teaches a rule of the world (naming one of the setting's internal terms), shows a dynamic between at least two named people who appear in it, or establishes how the setting works. A note says how. Non-clue paper is never padding.
checks.KT-MD-01: Each media declaration is valid: a known media form that can dress this document form, a valid date, people and places it may show, the right camera or publication, a time where the artifact prints one, handling and storage in range, and every required text region mapped to one of this document's S3 placeholders.
checks.KT-MD-02: Media stays within the case caps: artifacts, generated images (plates) and video logs.
checks.KT-MD-03: Everyone shown in a photograph, badge or video has a fixed appearance in the bible, so they look the same in every image.
checks.KT-MD-04: A media document carries every value its artifact shows (numbers, dates, names, imprints), copied exactly, so everything visible is also in the text.
checks.KT-MD-05: No document invents a number in one of the case's series (report, badge, message, specimen, chart, drawing or tape numbers). Every such number is one the kit calculated.
checks.KT-MD-06: Every weekday written next to a full date is the right weekday for that date.
checks.KT-MD-07: The media environment is valid: a known climate and hemisphere, a usable institution code, cameras that existed in the case's years, and publications with a name, founding date and cadence.
checks.KT-MD-08: A declared anomaly is deliberate: it changes one value the artifact shows, carries one of the document's facts, and really differs from the calculated value.
checks.KT-MD-09: Depiction placeholders belong to a media depiction region of the same document and never appear in the engine case.
checks.VL-17: An assessment uses none of its voice profile's signature words. Soft warning.
checks.KT-AU-01: The audit agent is not configured, or is declared as the same model family as the authoring agent.
checks.KT-AU-02: The audit answer file is missing or does not match its schema.
checks.AU-01: The blind solver must pick the correct option for every question.
checks.AU-02: Every document the blind solver cites for a question must be valid for that answer, and together they must cover every fact the answer rests on.
checks.AU-03: With only the questions and options, the shortcut probe must not find the correct answer above chance plus the margin.
checks.KT-BI-16: Each embraced trope needs a known lens ID and a plain account of how the lens renews it, within the limit on embraced tropes.
